paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption_used: The effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. Six model configurations are compared across nine language families: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The IE-Indic family shows the largest effects overall, with most configurations reaching between 17 and 25, while Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. Notably, IE-Germanic exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, suggesting high variability, and the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) dominate over the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large.
model_annotation: This grouped vertical bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks across nine language families for six distinct model configurations. The horizontal axis contains the categories, labeled "family," and displays the language families in alphabetical order from left to right: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis is labeled "effect" and uses a linear scale with numeric tick labels and corresponding horizontal gridlines at intervals of 10, from 0 to 30, though the plotted data and error bars extend slightly below 0 and up to 35. Within each language family on the horizontal axis, the six model configurations are plotted side-by-side as a grouped set of bars. According to the legend positioned on the right, these components are distinguished by color: mBERT-L$_2$ is light blue, XLM-L$_2$ is dark blue, mBERT-R$_2$ is light green, XLM-R$_2$ is dark green, mBERT-B$_2$ is light red, and XLM-B$_2$ is dark red. Every bar features a thin black outline and is annotated with a black vertical error bar with caps indicating standard deviation. Bar heights vary considerably across the categories; the tallest individual bars appear in the IE-Indic family, where mBERT-B$_2$ reaches approximately 24 and XLM-B$_2$ reaches roughly 21. In contrast, the shortest bars are found in the Isolate and Uralic families, where all six configurations yield effects very close to zero. A few bars fall below the zero baseline, notably the mBERT-R$_2$ and XLM-R$_2$ configurations in the Semitic family, which sit at approximately -2 and -1. The Semitic family also exhibits expansive error bars, with the XLM-B$_2$ configuration's upper error bar extending to the overall maximum height of 35. In the IE-Germanic group, the mBERT-B$_2$ and XLM-B$_2$ bars both reach approximately 15, while in IE-Slavic, these same B2 variants measure about 17 and 15, respectively.
